issues.legal_issue: A claimant’s standing to challenge the cancellation of a local-area body’s status is not lost merely because the claimant’s membership of that body ends after the challenge is filed.
material_facts: The claimants were members of local-area committees when they filed their petitions challenging the government’s cancellation of the notifications that established the committees.
The cancellation affected rights the claimants held under the governing scheme.
The claimants’ committee terms later expired, and they also had an interest as inhabitants in the continuation of the local status conferred on their areas.
issues.conclusion: The claimants had standing to pursue their challenge; the later end of their committee membership did not remove it.
issues.legal_principle: A person whose statutory rights are affected by a decision may challenge it, and the later end of that person’s office does not extinguish standing to pursue the challenge. A continuing interest as an inhabitant of the affected area also supports standing.

rule.if: challenge_to_government_cancellation and ((member_when_challenge_filed and rights_affected) or inhabitant_with_continuing_interest)

predicates.challenge_to_government_cancellation: A claimant brings a proceeding challenging the government’s cancellation of a local-area body’s status.
predicates.member_when_challenge_filed: The claimant was a member of the affected local-area body when the challenge was filed.
predicates.rights_affected: The government’s cancellation affected rights the claimant held under the governing scheme.
predicates.inhabitant_with_continuing_interest: The claimant lives in the affected area and has an ongoing interest in its local status.
predicates.claimant_has_standing: The claimant is entitled to pursue the challenge.

issues.definition: When a claimant challenges the government’s cancellation of a local-area body’s status, the claimant may pursue the challenge if the claimant was a member whose rights were affected when it was filed or has a continuing interest as an inhabitant.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory power to cancel or modify the designation and administrative arrangements of a local area is not arbitrary merely because the provision granting that power does not itself enumerate every circumstance for its exercise, where the surrounding statutory scheme supplies guiding principles.
material_facts: The challenge argued that the power to cancel or modify a local-area designation or related administrative order was arbitrary and undirected because the provision conferring it stated no circumstances or guidelines for its use.

The surrounding statutory scheme allowed a local area to receive a degree of local autonomy and administrative powers suited to its circumstances, rather than necessarily being constituted as a full municipality.
The scheme contemplated that local arrangements could change as an area’s economic viability and administrative capacity developed or proved inadequate.

The challenge before the Court concerned the validity of the statutory power, not whether the cancellation in any particular case was justified; allegations of mala fides and extraneous considerations had been abandoned.
issues.conclusion: The cancellation and modification power was valid and did not violate the constitutional guarantee of equality; the Court did not decide whether any particular cancellation was justified.
issues.legal_principle: The statutory provision must be read with the related provisions governing the same subject, rather than in isolation. The Court applied Article 14 and read the power in light of the scheme governing local autonomy and its gradual evolution according to economic and administrative viability. It approved Gram Sabha Begowal v. State of Punjab, which found sufficient guidance in the related scheme, and distinguished State of Punjab v. Dewan Chand because that case concerned a different statutory scheme. The Court did not decide the validity of any particular cancellation.

predicates.constitutional_validity_challenge: A proceeding challenges the constitutional validity of a statutory power to cancel or modify a local area’s designation or administrative arrangements.
predicates.surrounding_scheme_sets_local_autonomy_c: The surrounding statutory scheme sets circumstances for granting a local area limited autonomy and administrative powers suited to its needs.
predicates.cancellation_power_adjusts_administratio: The cancellation or modification power enables the government to adjust local administration as the area’s economic viability or administrative capacity changes.
predicates.cancellation_power_is_not_arbitrary_or_i: The statutory cancellation or modification power is not arbitrary or constitutionally invalid.

issues.definition: A challenged cancellation or modification power is not arbitrary or invalid when the surrounding scheme guides the grant of local autonomy and the power allows administration to respond to changes in the area’s economic or administrative viability.
